anomalies.observed: In the POWER TRAIN 'Reverse polarity protection' block, the series high-side switch T8 is populated with an AON6407 (an N-channel MOSFET). Its gate is pulled to GND through R33 (33 k) and clamped to the input node by the 12 V zener D5, and the body-diode/terminal orientation drawn is that of a P-channel ideal-diode switch (source referenced to the +24 V input, gate held near 0 V).
anomalies.expected: A high-side series reverse-polarity/ideal-diode FET whose gate is referenced to ground through R33 and clamped by a gate-source zener must be a P-channel device (the reference r1 build used the SI2301 P-MOSFET for this function). An N-channel part placed here has Vgs ≈ -24 V (gate at 0 V, source at +24 V), which exceeds its ±20 V gate-source rating and cannot turn the device on, so the 24 V rail never energizes (or only passes current through a body diode oriented opposite the intended direction).

evidence.quote: POWER TRAIN > Reverse polarity protection: T8 'AON6407' in series on the +24V path, gate to GND via R33 33k, D5 12V zener from gate to input (sheet 1/1, region A1-B1)
T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch
r1's BOM lists general-purpose switching transistors only (T1 SI2301 P-MOSFET, T2/T6 BT3904, T3/T5/T7/T8 AO3400A ×4, T4 IRLR2905)

anomalies.impact: The 24 V input rail fails to come up (or is forced through a reverse-oriented body diode with gate-oxide overstress), so the buck, LDO, ESP32 and all sensors/actuators are dead — the board does not power on at all.

parsed.summary: The schematic otherwise matches the specification's topology and values (buck/LDO rails, 2.2 k I2C pull-ups, 110 mΩ current-sense, 2 k2 isolated pull-ups, DNP environmental sensors, float-switch interlocks). The one deviation is the high-side reverse-polarity switch T8, drawn with a P-channel ideal-diode topology (gate pulled to GND via R33, 12 V gate-source zener D5) but populated with an N-channel AON6407, which cannot turn on and will prevent the 24 V rail from energizing.
